sara_support: :rotating_light: customer report — Go SDK (JSON mode, streaming) failing to parse some responses during bursts. They see errors like `invalid character '\u' in string escape` followed by `unexpected EOF`. Happening on /v1/responses (json mode) with large streaming outputs. Attaching minimal logs below.

```
> 2026-03-01T14:12:03Z ERROR go-sdk: decoder error: invalid character '\u' in string escape
> 2026-03-01T14:12:03Z WARN  go-sdk: read bytes: 128, remaining connection open
> 2026-03-01T14:12:03Z ERROR go-sdk: decode failed: unexpected EOF
```

sara_support: Customer using go-sdk v0.12.1, Linux, Dedicated region-us-west-2. Error rate spikes during heavy token bursts (~10% of streams). Can someone triage? @alex_dev

alex_dev: Thanks — can you paste a minimal repro or a snippet of what the streaming body looks like? Also confirm if the upstream model emits non-BMP characters (surrogate pairs) or long escaped sequences.

jin_qa: I reproduced locally with a tiny server that sends a JSON object in two writes, intentionally splitting a UTF-16 escape across the boundary. Repro program (Go):

```
// tiny server to reproduce split escape
http.HandleFunc("/repro", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
  w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
  // first chunk: partial surrogate pair
  w.Write([]byte(`{"msg":"emoji:\uD83D`))
  time.Sleep(50 * time.Millisecond)
  // second chunk: the rest
  w.Write([]byte(`\uDE00"}`))
})
// client: json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&out)
```

jin_qa: Using the standard library json.Decoder against that stream returns `invalid character '\u' in string escape` because the decoder sees a truncated `\u` sequence at the moment it processes the buffer.

maria_eng: This rings true — json.Decoder operates on the bytes currently buffered and can fail when an escape sequence is split across TCP chunks. We've hit similar issues in other SDKs when relying solely on stream decoding without lightweight buffering. Two options: (1) accumulate until you have a full JSON object (simple framing), or (2) implement a small buffer in the SDK decoder to hold partial tokens up to N bytes before attempting decode.

maria_eng: Workaround for customers: wrap resp.Body with bufio.NewReaderSize(resp.Body, 64*1024) and use json.Decoder on that reader, or use a tiny framing layer that waits for balanced braces when using NDJSON-like streams.

alex_dev: Thanks @jin_qa and @maria_eng — actionable plan: I'll add a buffered wrapper in go-sdk v0.12.x that reads into an internal buffer up to 64KB or until a complete top-level JSON value is available. If the stream is NDJSON we already support line-delimited framing; this will target the JSON-mode streaming case where the server sends raw JSON object-by-object without explicit line delimiters.

alex_dev: Short-term patch: detect `invalid character '\u' in string escape` errors and retry the decoder after reading an extra chunk (up to 4 retries). Long-term: proper buffer + heuristics for surrogate/escape boundaries.

opsbot: Incident created: INC-2026-4823 — "go-sdk jsonmode streaming: split escape leads to decoding failures" assigned to eng-runtime oncall.

sara_support: Customer accepted the workaround (bufio wrapper) but asked for a stable SDK fix and a timeline. They also noted a billing impact since many streams retried and incurred duplicate tokens. Logged a billing ticket to evaluate credits for affected windows.

maria_eng: I'll coordinate with billing. alex_dev, please post a PR link and ETA here when available. Marking this Escalated -> eng-runtime and tagging in the weekly ship. :white_check_mark:

alex_dev: Will open PR today: go-sdk#fix-jsonmode-buffering, target patch release v0.12.2 within 3 days. I'll add unit tests that simulate split-escape chunks and a minimal e2e repro harness.

sara_support: Great — keeping customer updated. Closing the support thread once patch is released.
